findings.description: The `finally` clause runs after both the success and failure paths, so `job.next_run = now + job.interval` always replaces the value set in the except branch (`now + self._retry_delay(job)`). The new retry/backoff feature therefore has no effect: failed jobs are rescheduled a full interval later, exactly as before. `retry_delay` is validated and documented but never used in practice.
findings.suggestion: Set `job.next_run = now + job.interval` only in the `else` branch (success path) and drop the `finally`, so the failure path keeps its backoff-based next_run.
findings.title: finally block overwrites the retry backoff next_run

findings.description: `job.retry_delay * 2 ** (consecutive_failures - 1)` grows without bound if `max_failures` is large. A huge multiplier makes timedelta multiplication raise OverflowError before `min` caps it. That exception escapes `_run`'s except block, so the record is never appended and `tick` aborts.
findings.suggestion: Cap the exponent, for example `min(consecutive_failures - 1, 30)`, or compute the delay iteratively and stop once it reaches `job.interval`.
findings.title: Unbounded exponent in backoff computation can overflow
